readings.title: A People Who Refuse to Return
readings.subtitle: Judah's Persistent Apostasy
readings.text: [Jeremiah 8:4] “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Would they fall, and not rise? Does one turn away and not return?</dq> [5] <dq>“Why then has this people, Yerushalayim, turned away in a continual backsliding? They are strengthened in deceit, they refuse to turn back.</dq> [6] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have listened and heard – they do not speak right. No man has repented of his evil, saying, ‘What have <dn>I</dn> done?’ They all turned to their own course, like a horse rushing into battle.</dq> [7] <dq>“Even a stork in the heavens knows her appointed times. And a turtledove, and a swallow, and a thrush guard <dn>את</dn> the time of their coming. But <dn>My</dn> people do not know <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“How do you say, ‘We are wise, and the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with us’? But look, the false pen of the scribe has worked falsehood.</dq> [9] <dq>“The wise shall be put to shame, they shall be broken down and caught. See, they have rejected <dn>את</dn> the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so what wisdom do they have?</dq> [10] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> give their wives to others, and their fields to possessing ones. For from the least even to the greatest, they are all greedy for gain. From the prophet to the priest, all act falsely.</dq> [11] <dq>“And they heal <dn>את</dn> the breach of the daughter of <dn>My</dn> people slightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace!’ when there is no peace.</dq> [12] <dq>“Were they ashamed when they had done abomination? No! They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to blush. So they shall fall among those who fall. They shall stumble in the time of their visitation,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall snatch them away,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“There are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has faded. And what <dn>I</dn> gave them shall pass away from them.” ’ ”</dq> [14] Why are we sitting still? Gather yourselves, and let us go into the walled cities, and let us be silent there. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> has let us perish and given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] We looked for peace, but there was no good; and for a time of healing, but see – fear! [16] The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan All the land shook at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones. They came and devoured the land and all that fills it, the city and those who dwell in it. [17] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am sending among you serpents, adders, which have no enchanter, and they shall bite you,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Prophet's Anguish
readings.subtitle: No Balm in Gilead
readings.text: [Jeremiah 8:18] When in grief I would seek comfort; my heart is sick within me. [19] Observe! The voice, the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land, “Is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> not in Tsiyon? Is her Sovereign not in her?” <dq>“Why have they provoked <dn>Me</dn> with their carved images, and with foreign worthlessnesses?”</dq> [20] “The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we have not been saved!” [21] For the breach of the daughter of my people I have been broken. I have grown sad; astonishment has taken hold of me. [22] Is there no balm in Gil‛aḏ, is there no healer there? Why has the healing of the daughter of my people not come? [Jeremiah 9:1] Oh, that my head were waters, and my eyes a fountain of tears, and I would weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people! [2] Oh, that I had in the wilderness a lodging place for wayfaring men, and I would leave my people, and go from them! For they are all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.

readings.title: A Nation of Deceit
readings.subtitle: Judgment for Forsaking the Torah
readings.text: [Jeremiah 9:3] <dq>“And they bend their tongue like a bow. Falsehood, and not truth, prevails on the earth. For they proceed from evil to evil, and they have not known <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] <dq>“Let everyone beware of his neighbour and not trust any brother. For every brother catches by the heel, and every neighbour walks with slanderers.</dq> [5] <dq>“And everyone deceives his neighbour, and no one speaks the truth. They have taught their tongue to speak falsehood, and have wearied themselves to crook.</dq> [6] <dq>“You live in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> shall refine them, and shall try them, for what shall <dn>I</dn> do because of the daughter of <dn>My</dn> people?</dq> [8] <dq>“Their tongue is a slaying arrow. It speaks deceit – speaks peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth, but in his heart he sets his ambush.</dq> [9] <dq>“Would <dn>I</dn> not punish them for this?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Would <dn>I</dn> not revenge <dn>Myself</dn> on such a nation as this?”</dq> [10] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall take up a weeping and wailing for the mountains, and for the pastures of the wilderness a lamentation, because they have been burned up, without any passing over, nor has the voice of cattle been heard. Both the birds of the heavens and the beasts have fled, they have gone.</dq> [11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim a heap of ruins, a habitation for jackals; and <dn>את</dn> the cities of Yehuḏah <dn>I</dn> shall make a waste, without an inhabitant.”</dq> [12] Who is the wise man, that he understands this? And to whom has the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoken, that he declares it? Why has the land perished, has it been burned up like a wilderness, with none passing through? [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says, <dq>“Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Torah which <dn>I</dn> set before them, and have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice, nor walked according to it,</dq> [14] <dq>but they have walked according to the stubbornness of their own heart and after the Ba‛als, which their fathers had taught them.”</dq> [15] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am making this people eat wormwood, and <dn>I</dn> shall make them drink poisoned water.</dq> [16] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter them among the nations, whom neither they nor their fathers have known. And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> a sword after them until <dn>I</dn> have consumed them.”</dq>

readings.title: A Call for Mourning
readings.subtitle: Boast Only in Knowing YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Jeremiah 9:17] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Discern! And call for the mourning women, that they come. And send for the wise women, that they come.</dq> [18] <dq>“And let them hasten and take up a wailing for us, and let our eyes run with tears and our eyelids gush with water.</dq> [19] <dq>“For a voice of wailing is heard from Tsiyon, ‘How we are ravaged! We are greatly ashamed, because we have forsaken the land, because we have been thrown out of our dwellings.’ ”</dq> [20] <dq>But hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O women, and let your ear receive <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>His</dn> mouth. And teach your daughters wailing, and each one her neighbour a lamentation.</dq> [21] <dq>For death has come through our windows, has entered our palaces, cutting off the children from the streets, and the young men from the squares.</dq> [22] Speak, <dq>“Thus declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘The corpses of men shall fall as dung on the face of the field, like cuttings after the reaper, with none to gather them.’ ”</dq> [23] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Let not the wise boast in his wisdom, let not the mighty boast in his might, nor let the rich boast in his riches,</dq> [24] <dq>but let him who boasts boast of this, that he understands and knows <dn>Me</dn>, that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, doing loving-commitment, right-ruling, and righteousness in the earth. For in these <dn>I</dn> delight,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [25] <dq>“See, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when <dn>I</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> all circumcised with the uncircumcised –</dq> [26] <dq>“Mitsrayim, and Yehuḏah, and Eḏom, and the children of Ammon, and Mo’aḇ, and all those trimmed on the edges, who dwell in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Yisra’ěl are uncircumcised in heart!”</dq>

readings.title: The Living Elohim vs. Worthless Idols
readings.subtitle: Do Not Learn the Way of the Nations
readings.text: [Jeremiah 10:1] Hear <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks to you, O house of Yisra’ěl. [2] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Do not learn <dn>את</dn> the way of the nations, and do not be awed by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are awed by them.</dq> [3] <dq>“For the laws of these peoples are worthless, for one cuts a tree from the forest, work for the hands of a craftsman with a cutting tool.</dq> [4] <dq>“They beautify it with silver and gold, they strengthen it with nails and hammers so that it does not topple.</dq> [5] <dq>“They are like a rounded post, and they do not speak. They have to be carried, because they do not walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they do no evil, nor is it in them to do any good.”</dq> [6] There is none like You, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. You are great, and great is Your Name in might. [7] Who would not fear You, O Sovereign of the nations? For this is Your due, for among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their reigns, there is none like You. [8] They are both brutish and foolish, an instruction of worthlessness is the tree. [9] Silver is beaten into plates; it is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the craftsman and of the hands of the smith; draped in blue and purple; all of them are the work of skilled ones. [10] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is truly <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>He</dn> is the living <dn>Elohim</dn> and the everlasting Sovereign. At <dn>His</dn> wrath the earth shakes, and nations are unable to stand <dn>His</dn> displeasure. [11] <dq>Say to them this, “The elah that did not make <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens.”</dq> [12] <dn>He</dn> has made <dn>את</dn> the earth by <dn>His</dn> power, <dn>He</dn> has established the world by <dn>His</dn> wisdom, and has stretched out <dn>את</dn> the heavens by <dn>His</dn> understanding. [13] When <dn>He</dn> makes <dn>His</dn> voice heard, there is a roaring of waters in the heavens. And <dn>He</dn> makes vapours rise from the ends of the earth. The lightnings for rain <dn>He</dn> has made, and brings wind from <dn>His</dn> treasuries. [14] Everyone is brutish in knowledge; every smith is put to shame by his idol. For his moulded image is falsehood, and there is no spirit in them. [15] They are worthless, a work of mockery. In the time of their punishment they perish. [16] The Portion of Ya‛aqoḇ is not like these, for <dn>He</dn> is the Maker of all, and Yisra’ěl is the tribe of <dn>His</dn> inheritance – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name.

readings.title: Impending Exile
readings.subtitle: Gather Your Belongings from the Land
readings.text: [Jeremiah 10:17] Gather up your bundle from the ground, you who live under siege! [18] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, at this time <dn>I</dn> am hurling out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the land, and shall distress them, so that they feel it.”</dq> [19] Woe to me for my breaking! My wound is grievous, but I say, “This is my sickness, and I bear it. [20] “My tent has been ravaged, and all my cords have been broken. My children have gone from me, and they are no more. There is no one to pitch my tent any more, or to set up my curtains. [21] For the shepherds have become brutish, and they have not sought <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Therefore they did not understand, and all their flock scattered.” [22] See, it has come, the voice of a report, and a great shaking out of the land of the north, to make the cities of Yehuḏah a waste, a habitation of jackals.

readings.title: Jeremiah's Plea for Just Correction
readings.subtitle: Pour Out Your Wrath on the Nations
readings.text: [Jeremiah 10:23] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> know the way of man is not in himself, it is not for man who walks to direct his own steps. [24] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, chastise me, but with right-ruling – not in Your displeasure, lest You bring me to naught. [25] Pour out Your wrath on the nations who do not know You, and on the tribes who do not call on Your Name. For they have eaten up <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ, devoured him and consumed him, and laid waste his home.

readings.title: The Covenant is Broken
readings.subtitle: A Green Olive Tree Set on Fire
readings.text: [Jeremiah 11:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [2] <dq>“Hear <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Yehuḏah and to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.</dq> [3] <dq>“And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “Cursed is the man who does not obey <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant,</dq> [4] <dq>which <dn>I</dn> commanded your fathers in the day when <dn>I</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the iron furnace, saying, ‘Obey <dn>My</dn> voice, and you shall do according to all that <dn>I</dn> command you, and you shall be <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> be your <dn>Elohim</dn>,’</dq> [5] <dq>in order to establish <dn>את</dn> the oath which <dn>I</dn> have sworn to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.” ’ ”</dq> And <dn>I</dn> answered and said, “Aměn, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Proclaim <dn>את</dn> all these words in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the streets of Yerushalayim, saying, ‘Hear <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant and do them.</dq> [7] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> earnestly warned your fathers in the day that <dn>I</dn> brought them up out of the land of Mitsrayim, until this day, rising early and warning, saying, “Obey <dn>My</dn> voice.”</dq> [8] <dq>But they did not obey or incline their ear, but everyone walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So <dn>I</dn> brought on them <dn>את</dn> all the words of this covenant, which <dn>I</dn> commanded them to do, and they did not do.’ ”</dq> [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“There is a conspiracy among the men of Yehuḏah and among the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.</dq> [10] <dq>“They have turned back to the crookednesses of their forefathers who refused to hear <dn>My</dn> words, and they have gone after other mighty ones to serve them. The house of Yisra’ěl and the house of Yehuḏah have broken <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant <dn>I</dn> made with their fathers.”</dq> [11] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil on them which they are unable to escape. Then they shall cry out to <dn>Me</dn>, but <dn>I</dn> shall not listen to them.</dq> [12] <dq>“And the cities of Yehuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim shall go and cry out to the mighty ones to whom they burn incense, but they shall bring no deliverance to them at all in the time of their evil.</dq> [13] <dq>“For your mighty ones have become as many as your cities, O Yehuḏah. And you have set up as many slaughter-places to shame as there are streets in Yerushalayim – slaughter-places to burn incense to Ba‛al.</dq> [14] <dq>“And you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer for them, for <dn>I</dn> do not hear them in the time that they cry out to <dn>Me</dn> because of their evil.</dq> [15] <dq>“Why should <dn>My</dn> beloved be in <dn>My</dn> house – she has done wickedness with many. And does the set-apart flesh remove your evil from you? Then you rejoice?</dq> [16] <dq>“<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has named you, ‘Green Olive Tree, Beautiful, of Goodly Fruit.’ With the noise of a great sound <dn>He</dn> has set it on fire, and its branches shall be broken.</dq> [17] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, who planted you, has spoken evil against you for the evil of the house of Yisra’ěl and of the house of Yehuḏah, which they have done against themselves to provoke <dn>Me</dn>, by burning incense to Ba‛al.”</dq>

readings.title: The Plot Against Jeremiah
readings.subtitle: Judgment on the Men of Anathoth
readings.text: [Jeremiah 11:18] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made it known to me, and <dn>I</dn> know it. Then You showed me their deeds. [19] But I was like a gentle lamb brought to the slaughter. And I did not know that they had plotted against me, saying, “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more.” [20] But, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, who judges righteously, who tries kidneys and heart, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for unto You <dn>I</dn> have revealed my cause. [21] “Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the men of Anathoth who are seeking your life, saying, ‘Do not prophesy in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lest you die by our hand’ – [22] therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am punishing them, the young men shall die by the sword, their sons and their daughters shall die by scarcity of food.</dq> [23] <dq>And there shall be no remnant of them, for <dn>I</dn> bring evil on the men of Anathoth – the year of their punishment.’ ”</dq>
